question:
Assertion (A): The Palas are remembered as great patrons of Buddhist education.

Reason (R): Dharmapala founded Vikramashila and revived Nalanda, while Gopala founded Odantapuri.

Choose the correct option.
option_1: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true but R is false
option_4: A is false but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both A and R are true and R explains A: the Palas patronised Buddhist learning because Dharmapala founded Vikramashila and revived Nalanda, and Gopala founded Odantapuri (पाल — बौद्ध शिक्षा के संरक्षक)

 

• Three major Buddhist universities of Bihar thus owed their growth to Pala rulers.

 

• Pala patronage drew scholars and students from Tibet, China and South-East Asia to these monasteries.

 

• The universities declined after the Pala dynasty weakened and Bakhtiyar Khilji raided Bihar.

 

• As patrons of Mahayana and Vajrayana Buddhism the Palas continued the tradition of royal support given earlier by Ashoka and Harsha, in an age when Buddhism was losing ground in most of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nalanda was originally a Gupta-age foundation.

 

• Vikramashila was a centre of Tantric Buddhism.

 

• Odantapuri was in Magadha.

 

• Pala patronage extended to Buddhist art and manuscript painting.

 

• Pala monasteries kept close ties with Tibet, and many Sanskrit Buddhist texts survive only in Tibetan translations made through this connection, which preserved Indian learning after the monasteries were destroyed in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 2): This choice says R does not explain A, which is wrong. The foundation and revival of the three universities directly shows why the Palas are called patrons of Buddhist education.

 

• A is true but R is false (Option 3): This choice calls R false, but the facts that Dharmapala founded Vikramashila and Gopala founded Odantapuri are in the notes and are correct.

 

• A is false but R is true (Option 4): This choice calls A false, but the Pala dynasty is known precisely for its support to Buddhist monasteries and learning.

question:
Assertion (A): Mihir Bhoj is regarded as the most famous ruler of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty.

Reason (R): Under him the Pratihara kingdom had its capital at Kannauj and reached its greatest power.

Choose the correct option.
option_1: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_2: A is true but R is false
option_3: A is false but R is true
option_4: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both A and R are true and R explains A: Mihir Bhoj is called the real founder and most famous ruler of the Gurjara-Pratihara line because under him Kannauj was the capital and the empire reached its height (मिहिर भोज — प्रतिहार वंश का महान शासक)

 

• His rule is placed in the ninth century, when the Pratiharas dominated much of northern India.

 

• He was an important participant in the tripartite struggle for Kannauj against the Palas and Rashtrakutas.

 

• He took the title Adivaraha, as shown on his coins and inscriptions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty is placed in the 8th to 11th century in the notes.

 

• Nagabhata I is said to have founded the line.

 

• Mihir Bhoj must not be confused with Raja Bhoj of the Paramara dynasty.

 

• His son Mahendrapala I continued the empire.

 

• Mihir Bhoj's reign is placed between about 836 and 885 AD, and he was followed by his son Mahendrapala I, so he ruled for close to half a century, which gave the empire unusual stability.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 1): This choice says R is not a valid explanation of A, but the height of power and the capital at Kannauj are exactly why Bhoj is regarded as the greatest Pratihara ruler.

 

• A is true but R is false (Option 2): This choice calls R false, but the Pratiharas under Bhoj did rule from Kannauj and reached their peak of power. R is a correct statement.

 

• A is false but R is true (Option 3): This choice calls A false, but Mihir Bhoj is the famous ruler of the Pratihara line and is even called its real founder in the notes.

question: Which Pratihara ruler successfully repelled Arab invasions in North-Western India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagabhata I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nagabhata I of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty checked the advance of the Arabs from Sindh into north-western India, and the notes name him as the founder of the Pratihara line (नागभट्ट प्रथम — अरब आक्रमण को रोका)

 

• Pratihara resistance kept Arab rule confined to Sindh and Multan, and they did not spread further into the Indian interior.

 

• This gave the Pratiharas the reputation of being protectors of western India against foreign invaders.

 

• Their power later centred on Kannauj, which became the capital under Mihir Bhoj.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Arab forces had conquered Sindh in 712 AD under Muhammad bin Qasim.

 

• The Rashtrakutas also resisted the Arabs in the Deccan and Gujarat.

 

• Nagabhata II later took Kannauj.

 

• The Pratiharas were called Gurjara-Pratiharas.

 

• Arab writers called the Gurjara-Pratihara kingdom Juzr and described its cavalry as among the strongest armies of India, which agrees with the Indian tradition of the Pratiharas as defenders of the west.

 

NOTE

 

• Mihira Bhoja (Option 1): Mihira Bhoja was the greatest Pratihara ruler of the ninth century and made Kannauj his capital. He came after the Arab threat had been checked and is not credited with the repulse.

 

• Rajyapala (Option 2): Rajyapala was a late Pratihara king of the early eleventh century who lost Kannauj to Mahmud of Ghazni. He had no role in checking the Arabs.

 

• Vatsaraja (Option 4): Vatsaraja was an eighth-century Pratihara ruler who was defeated by the Rashtrakuta king Dhruva in the contest for Kannauj. The Arab repulse is credited to Nagabhata I.

question: The Arab traveller Al-Masudi visited India in 915 AD during the reign of which Gurjara-Pratihara ruler?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahipala I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Al-Masudi visited India in 915 AD during the reign of the Pratihara ruler Mahipala I, the son of Mahendrapala, and described the extent of Pratihara power (अल-मसूदी की यात्रा — 915 ई., महिपाल प्रथम)

 

• Mahipala I ruled in the early tenth century when the Pratihara empire was still large but beginning to weaken.

 

• Soon after, the Rashtrakuta ruler Indra III raided Kannauj, which marked the decline of Pratihara power.

 

• Al-Masudi's account is an important foreign source for the Pratihara period, like Hiuen Tsang for the age of Harsha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Al-Masudi was an Arab historian and geographer from Baghdad.

 

• Mahipala I's father was Mahendrapala I.

 

• Mihir Bhoj ruled in the ninth century.

 

• Alberuni wrote Kitab-ul-Hind in the eleventh century.

 

• Al-Masudi's Muruj al-Dhahab, the Meadows of Gold, describes the Pratihara king as holding a vast army arranged in four divisions for the four directions, a detail that shows the military scale of the empire.

 

NOTE

 

• Mihir Bhoj (Option 1): Mihir Bhoj ruled earlier, in the ninth century, and was the grandfather of Mahipala I. The visit of Al-Masudi in 915 AD falls in the later reign of Mahipala I.

 

• Nagabhata I (Option 2): Nagabhata I belongs to the eighth century, about two centuries before 915 AD. He is known for resisting the Arabs, not for hosting Al-Masudi.

 

• Vatsaraja (Option 3): Vatsaraja was an eighth-century ruler defeated by Dhruva. He lived long before Al-Masudi arrived, and his fame rests on his defeat by the Rashtrakuta king Dhruva in the struggle for Kannauj.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Gurjara-Pratiharas:

1. Mihir Bhoj founded the Vikramashila University.

2. Nagabhata I founded the Pratihara line.

3. Al-Masudi visited India in 915 AD during the reign of Mahipala I.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 2 and 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statements 2 and 3 hold true: Nagabhata I founded the Pratihara line and Al-Masudi visited in 915 AD under Mahipala I; statement 1 is wrong because Vikramashila was founded by the Pala ruler Dharmapala (प्रतिहार — नागभट्ट प्रथम, अल-मसूदी 915 ई.)

 

• The Pratiharas and Palas were rivals in the tripartite struggle, so the two dynasties' institutions should not be mixed up.

 

• Mihir Bhoj's fame lies in military power and his capital at Kannauj, not in establishing a university.

 

• Vikramashila was a Buddhist centre of Bihar, a region ruled by the Palas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty is dated 8th to 11th century in the notes.

 

• Mahipala I was the son of Mahendrapala.

 

• Palas patronised Buddhist institutions.

 

• Mihir Bhoj took the title Adivaraha.

 

• The Gwalior Prashasti, a Sanskrit eulogy found at Gwalior in Madhya Pradesh, describes the exploits of Nagabhata II according to the notes, and it is a key inscriptional source for Pratihara history.

 

NOTE

 

• Only 1 and 2 (Option 1): This combination includes the false statement 1 and omits statement 3. Mihir Bhoj did not found Vikramashila, and Al-Masudi's visit in 915 AD is correct.

 

• Only 1 and 3 (Option 2): This combination keeps the false statement 1 and omits statement 2. Nagabhata I did found the Pratihara line, so statement 2 must be included.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): This combination says all three are correct, but statement 1 is false because Vikramashila belongs to the Pala king Dharmapala.

question: Which of the following is NOT a ruler of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gopala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gopala was the founder of the Pala dynasty of Bengal in about 750 AD, not a Pratihara ruler; Nagabhata I, Mihir Bhoj and Mahipala I all belong to the Gurjara-Pratiharas (गोपाल — पाल वंश का संस्थापक)

 

• The Pratiharas ruled from the 8th to the 11th century with Kannauj as a major centre, while the Palas ruled Bengal and Bihar.

 

• The two dynasties were rivals in the tripartite struggle with the Rashtrakutas.

 

• Since this is a NOT question, the ruler from the rival dynasty is the answer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mahipala I was the son of Mahendrapala I.

 

• Nagabhata I is credited with founding the Pratihara line.

 

• Al-Masudi visited during Mahipala I's reign in 915 AD.

 

• Gopala also founded Odantapuri University.

 

• Mahendrapala I, the son of Mihir Bhoj, carried the Pratihara empire into Magadha and Bengal and patronised the poet Rajashekhara, author of the Karpuramanjari and the Kavyamimamsa.

 

NOTE

 

• Nagabhata I (Option 1): Nagabhata I is the founder of the Pratihara line according to the notes and is credited with checking the Arabs. He is a Pratihara ruler, so he cannot be the exception.

 

• Mihir Bhoj (Option 3): Mihir Bhoj is the most famous Pratihara ruler, who made Kannauj his capital. Since he belongs to the dynasty, he is not the odd one out.

 

• Mahipala I (Option 4): Mahipala I was a Pratihara king, the son of Mahendrapala, in whose reign Al-Masudi came. He belongs to the dynasty and so cannot be the answer.

question: The Agnikula theory of Rajput origin is described in the Prithviraj Raso, written by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chandbardai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Agnikula (Agnikul Siddhant) theory of Rajput origin is given in the Prithviraj Raso by Chandbardai, the court poet of Prithviraj Chauhan (अग्निकुल सिद्धांत — पृथ्वीराज रासो, चंदबरदाई)

 

• The theory says the Rajputs arose from a sacrificial fire kindled by a sage at Mount Abu.

 

• It names four clans, Pratihar, Parmar, Chauhan and Solanki, and was probably a later attempt to give the Rajputs a sacred origin.

 

• The Rajput age is dated from about the 7th to the 12th century in the notes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Prithviraj Raso is an epic poem in an early form of Hindi or Brajbhasha.

 

• The work is a mixture of fact and legend and historians treat it with caution.

 

• The Rajputs emerged as ruling clans after the decline of the Gupta and Harsha empires.

 

• Chandbardai is said to have been Prithviraj's friend and poet.

 

NOTE

 

• Banabhatta (Option 1): Banabhatta was Harsha's court poet who wrote the Harshacharita and Kadambari. He lived centuries before the Rajput age and has no link with the Agnikula story.

 

• Kalhana (Option 2): Kalhana was the Kashmiri author of the Rajatarangini, the chronicle of the kings of Kashmir. He did not write the Prithviraj Raso.

 

• Jayanaka (Option 3): Jayanaka was the Kashmiri poet who wrote the Prithvirajavijaya, a Sanskrit work about the Chauhan king. The Agnikula legend in the notes comes from the Raso of Chandbardai.

question: According to the Agnikula theory, the sage Vashistha performed a yajna at which place from which the four Rajput clans arose?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mount Abu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the theory the sage Vashistha performed a sacrificial yajna at Mount Abu in Rajasthan, and four Rajput clans rose from the fire (माउंट आबू — अग्निकुंड, ऋषि वशिष्ठ)

 

• The four peoples produced were the Pratihar, Parmar, Chauhan and Solanki, associated with Kannauj, Malwa, Ajmer and Gujarat respectively in the notes.

 

• The story is found in the Prithviraj Raso and is a legend rather than historical evidence.

 

• The story was meant to raise the Rajputs to the status of Kshatriyas of fire-born origin.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mount Abu is the highest peak of the Aravalli range.

 

• The Dilwara Jain temples at Mount Abu were built in the Solanki period.

 

• Agnikula is the fire-born line, in contrast to the Suryavanshi and Chandravanshi lines.

 

• The Rajputs were also called Kshatriyas of the early medieval period.

 

• Mount Abu is the only hill station of Rajasthan, and Guru Shikhar at about 1722 metres is the highest peak of the Aravalli range, which is traditionally associated with the sage Dattatreya.

 

NOTE

 

• Kurukshetra (Option 1): Kurukshetra is the site of the Mahabharata war and of later battles of Thaneswar. It is not the place of the Agnikula yajna in the Rajput legend.

 

• Prayag (Option 2): Prayag, the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna, is known for Harsha's quinquennial assembly. It is not connected with the Agnikula story.

 

• Pushkar (Option 4): Pushkar in Rajasthan is a sacred lake and Brahma temple site, but the Agnikula legend places the fire sacrifice at Mount Abu.

question: Which of the following clans is NOT counted among the four Agnikula Rajput clans?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sisodia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The four Agnikula clans are Pratihar, Parmar, Chauhan and Solanki; the Sisodia clan of Mewar is not among them (सिसोदिया — अग्निकुल में शामिल नहीं)

 

• The Sisodias, a branch of the Guhilas of Mewar, claim descent from the Sun and are counted as Suryavanshi Rajputs.

 

• The Agnikula legend traces the four fire-born clans to the yajna at Mount Abu as narrated in the Prithviraj Raso.

 

• A NOT-type question requires the clan outside the list.

 

• Among Rajput clans the Guhilas of Mewar (Sisodias) and the Rathors claim descent from the Sun, whereas the Agnikula clans are those four said to have been produced from the sacrificial fire pit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rana Pratap and Rana Sanga were Sisodia rulers of Mewar.

 

• Chittorgarh was a major Sisodia centre.

 

• The Sisodias are traced to the Guhila line.

 

• Mewar was a leading Rajput kingdom in the Mughal period.

 

• The Guhila ruler Bappa Rawal is traditionally regarded as the founder of the Mewar line in the eighth century, and later Sisodia rulers such as Rana Kumbha and Rana Sanga made Mewar a major Rajput power.

 

NOTE

 

• Chauhan (Option 2): The Chauhans are one of the four Agnikula clans, linked in the notes with Ajmer. Since they belong in the list, they cannot be the answer.

 

• Parmar (Option 3): The Parmars are an Agnikula clan associated with Malwa, whose famous ruler was Raja Bhoj. They belong to the list and so are not the exception.

 

• Solanki (Option 4): The Solankis are the fourth Agnikula clan, linked with Gujarat in the notes. They are part of the four and so are not the answer.

question:
Match the Agnikula clans with their regions as given in the notes:

(a) Pratihar  (i) Gujarat

(b) Parmar  (ii) Ajmer

(c) Chauhan  (iii) Kannauj

(d) Solanki  (iv) Malwa
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct match is Pratihar - Kannauj, Parmar - Malwa, Chauhan - Ajmer and Solanki - Gujarat, i.e. a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i (राजपूत कुल — कन्नौज, मालवा, अजमेर, गुजरात)

 

• These four were the fire-born clans from the yajna of Vashistha at Mount Abu.

 

• The Chauhans ruled from Ajmer and the Solankis from Anhilwara in Gujarat.

 

• The Parmars held Malwa with Dhar as capital, and the Pratiharas later made Kannauj their capital.

 

• A simple order helps in recall: Pratihar, Parmar, Chauhan, Solanki go with Kannauj, Malwa, Ajmer and Gujarat in the same sequence as listed in the notes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Prithviraj Chauhan belonged to the Chauhan clan.

 

• Raja Bhoj belonged to the Parmar clan.

 

• Bhimdev I of the Solanki clan built the Modhera Sun Temple.

 

• Mihir Bhoj belonged to the Pratihara clan.

 

• Ajmer was the seat of the Chauhans (Chahamanas), Dhar the Paramara capital in Malwa, and Anhilwara the Solanki capital in Gujarat, so each clan in the notes has a recognisable centre of power.

 

NOTE

 

• a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii (Option 1): This combination gives Malwa to the Pratiharas and Kannauj to the Parmars, and also reverses Chauhan and Solanki. The Parmars ruled Malwa and the Pratihara capital was Kannauj.

 

• a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii (Option 3): This combination links the Pratiharas with Ajmer and the Parmars with Gujarat, which is wrong. Ajmer was Chauhan territory and Gujarat was Solanki territory.

 

• a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i (Option 4): This combination correctly joins the Pratiharas with Kannauj but gives Ajmer to the Parmars and Malwa to the Chauhans. These two pairs are reversed.

question:
Read the following statements:

1. After Harsha's death, the Rajputs rose to prominence in northern Indian politics.

2. The Rajputs maintained strong unity, which helped them resist foreign invasions effectively.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Only statement 1 is correct: after Harsha's death (647 AD) the Rajputs emerged as powerful rulers in north India, but they lacked political unity, which weakened resistance to foreign invasions (राजपूतों का उदय — हर्ष के बाद, एकता का अभाव)

 

• The Rajput age is dated from the 7th to the 12th century and saw many clans such as Pratiharas, Paramaras, Chauhans and Chandelas.

 

• These states fought one another constantly, as in the contests between the Chauhans and Chandelas.

 

• This disunity helped the Turkish invaders, such as Muhammad Ghori at Tarain, to defeat them one after another.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mahmud of Ghazni raided Rajput kingdoms in the early eleventh century.

 

• Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan in 1192 in the Second Battle of Tarain.

 

• Rajput kingdoms often failed to form a united front.

 

• The Pratihara decline led to many separate Rajput states.

 

• The Chauhan-Chandela rivalry is a famous example of Rajput disunity: Prithviraj Chauhan attacked the Chandela king Paramardideva at Mahoba in 1182, which weakened a possible ally against the Turkish invaders.

 

NOTE

 

• Only 2 (Option 1): This choice treats only statement 2 as correct and rejects statement 1, which is the reverse of the facts. The Rajputs did rise to prominence after Harsha, and they lacked unity.

 

• Both 1 and 2 (Option 2): This choice accepts statement 2 as well, but the Rajputs were divided by constant clan rivalries and did not resist foreign invaders with a united front. Statement 2 is therefore false.

 

• Neither 1 nor 2 is correct (Option 3): This choice calls both statements wrong, but statement 1 is a correct account of the rise of the Rajputs after the death of Harsha in 647 AD.

question:
Match the dynasties with their founders as given in the notes:

(a) Pala  (i) Samant Sen

(b) Gurjara-Pratihara  (ii) Aangpal

(c) Sena  (iii) Gopala

(d) Tomar  (iv) Nagabhatta I
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct pairs are Pala - Gopala, Gurjara-Pratihara - Nagabhatta I, Sena - Samant Sen and Tomar - Aangpal (Anangapala), i.e. a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii (राजवंश और संस्थापक)

 

• Gopala founded the Palas in 750 AD in Bengal, and Nagabhata I is credited with founding the Pratihara line.

 

• Samantasena began the Sena line in Bengal, and Anangapala is regarded as the founder of the Tomara line at Delhi.

 

• The Tomaras were later defeated by Prithviraj Chauhan.

 

• Founders are frequent SSC targets: Gopala (750 AD) for the Palas, Nagabhata I for the Pratiharas in the notes, Samantasena for the Senas and Anangapala for the Tomars at Delhi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Senas came to power in Bengal after the Palas.

 

• Dehliwal coins were issued by the Tomaras.

 

• Pratihara power centred on Kannauj under Mihir Bhoj.

 

• The Palas ruled for about four centuries.

 

• Vijayasena later raised the Senas to real prominence, and Ballalasena wrote the Danasagara and Adbhutasagara, so Samantasena is the early founder, while Anangapala's descendants held Delhi until Prithviraj Chauhan took it.

 

NOTE

 

• a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i (Option 2): This combination reverses the Pratihara and Pala founders and also the Sena and Tomar founders. Gopala belongs to the Palas and Samant Sen to the Senas.

 

• a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv (Option 3): This combination gives Samant Sen to the Palas and Aangpal to the Pratiharas, which is wrong. Aangpal belongs to the Tomaras and Samant Sen to the Senas.

 

• a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii (Option 4): This combination pairs the Palas with Gopala and the Tomars with Aangpal correctly, but swaps the Pratihara and Sena founders. Samant Sen belongs to the Senas and Nagabhata I founded the Pratihara line.

question: The Chandela dynasty ruled the Bundelkhand region, which in their time was known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jejak Bhukti.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Chandelas ruled Bundelkhand, then called Jejakabhukti (Jejak Bhukti), with Khajuraho and Mahoba as important centres (जेजाकभुक्ति — चंदेलों का क्षेत्र, बुंदेलखंड)

 

• The name Jejakabhukti comes from the Chandela ruler Jejaka or Jayashakti, according to later records.

 

• The Chandelas are best remembered for the Khajuraho temples built in the 10th-11th centuries.

 

• They were one of the Rajput dynasties that rose after the decline of the Gurjara-Pratiharas.

 

• Bundelkhand today covers parts of Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, so Khajuraho, Mahoba and Kalinjar all lie within the old Chandela heartland of Jejakabhukti.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kalinjar fort was a major Chandela stronghold.

 

• The Chandelas resisted Mahmud of Ghazni in the early eleventh century.

 

• Khajuraho was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

 

• Paramardideva was defeated by Prithviraj Chauhan and later by Qutbuddin Aibak.

 

• Khajuraho's temples were built between about 950 and 1050 AD by successive Chandela rulers, such as Yashovarman who built the Lakshmana temple and Dhanga who built the Vishvanatha temple.

 

NOTE

 

• Kamarupa (Option 1): Kamarupa was the ancient name of Assam and was ruled by Bhaskaravarman in Harsha's time. It is unrelated to Bundelkhand.

 

• Avanti (Option 2): Avanti was a Mahajanapada of the Malwa region with Ujjain as capital. It is not the Chandela territory, since Avanti lay in western Malwa and not in Bundelkhand, and it was ruled from Ujjain in the age of the Mahajanapadas.

 

• Vidarbha (Option 3): Vidarbha is the eastern part of present-day Maharashtra, far from Bundelkhand. It was never called Jejakabhukti, a name that belongs only to the Chandela region of Bundelkhand in central India, far to the north of Vidarbha.

question: The Kandariya Mahadev temple at Khajuraho, built by the Chandela king Vidyadhara, belongs to which style of temple architecture?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagara.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kandariya Mahadeva temple, built by Vidyadhara of the Chandela dynasty, is in the Nagara style of north India (कंदरिया महादेव मंदिर — नागर शैली)

 

• The Nagara style is marked by a tall curved shikhara over the sanctum and a high platform, typical of north Indian temples.

 

• The temple is famous for its rich sculpture on the walls, and it is dedicated to Shiva.

 

• Khajuraho's temples, built by the Chandelas, form a great group of Nagara temples.

 

• Khajuraho temples stand on a high platform (jagati) and have no boundary wall, unlike many south Indian temples that are enclosed within courtyards and gateways.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vesara is a mixture of the Nagara and Dravida styles seen in the Deccan.

 

• Dravida temples have a pyramidal vimana, typical of Tamil Nadu.

 

• Khajuraho is in Madhya Pradesh.

 

• Vidyadhara resisted Mahmud of Ghazni in the early eleventh century.

 

• The sculptures of Khajuraho show gods, apsaras, musicians and couples, and only a part of the carving is erotic, while the rest depicts daily life and the pleasures of the court.

 

NOTE

 

• Dravida (Option 2): Dravida is the south Indian style with a pyramidal tower over the sanctum, as at Thanjavur. The Khajuraho temples follow the northern tradition instead.

 

• Vesara (Option 3): Vesara is a hybrid of the Nagara and Dravida styles seen in the Deccan, particularly the Chalukyas and Hoysalas. The Khajuraho temple is a pure Nagara example.

 

• Gandhara (Option 4): Gandhara refers to a school of sculpture of the Kushan age that blended Greek and Indian art. It is not a style of temple architecture.

question: Which temple, built by the Chandela dynasty in the 10th-11th centuries, is known for its exquisite sculptures?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kandariya Mahadeva Temple.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kandariya Mahadeva Temple at Khajuraho was built by the Chandela dynasty in the 10th-11th centuries and is famed for its fine sculptures (कंदरिया महादेव मंदिर, खजुराहो — चंदेल)

 

• It stands in Madhya Pradesh in the Bundelkhand region once called Jejakabhukti.

 

• The temple belongs to the Nagara style and was built by Vidyadhara according to the notes.

 

• The Khajuraho group is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

 

• The Chandelas originally built about eighty-five temples at Khajuraho, of which about twenty-five survive today, and the western group containing Kandariya Mahadeva is the best known.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Khajuraho temples include the Lakshmana and Vishvanatha temples.

 

• The Chandelas ruled from Mahoba and Khajuraho.

 

• Brihadeeswarar is a Chola temple of the early eleventh century.

 

• The Modhera Sun Temple is a Solanki monument.

 

• Khajuraho was brought to the notice of the modern world in 1838 by the British engineer T S Burt, long after the Chandela capital had declined and the temples had been covered by forest.

 

NOTE

 

• Brihadeeswarar Temple (Option 1): The Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur was built by Rajaraja Chola I in the early eleventh century. It is a Dravida temple of the Cholas.

 

• Sun Temple, Modhera (Option 3): The Sun Temple at Modhera in Gujarat was built by the Solanki king Bhimdev I. It is not a Chandela temple.

 

• Lingaraja Temple (Option 4): The Lingaraja Temple at Bhubaneswar in Odisha belongs to the Kalinga tradition and the Ganga or Somavamshi period. It is not a Chandela monument.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Chandela dynasty:

1. They ruled the Bundelkhand region, called Jejak Bhukti.

2. The Kandariya Mahadev temple was built by Vidyadhara.

3. The Khajuraho temples were built in the Dravida style.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1 and 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Chandelas ruled Bundelkhand (Jejak Bhukti) and Vidyadhara built the Kandariya Mahadev temple; statement 3 is wrong because the Khajuraho temples are in the Nagara style (चंदेल — जेजाकभुक्ति, कंदरिया महादेव, नागर शैली)

 

• The Dravida style belongs to the south, with pyramidal towers, and was used by the Pallavas and Cholas.

 

• The Khajuraho temples have a curved shikhara and rich erotic and divine sculptures, typical of north Indian temples.

 

• The notes specifically describe the Kandariya Mahadev temple as a Nagara style building.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Khajuraho is a World Heritage Site.

 

• Vidyadhara was a Chandela ruler who opposed Mahmud of Ghazni.

 

• The Kailasa temple at Ellora is a Rashtrakuta monument.

 

• The Chandelas had strongholds at Kalinjar and Mahoba.

 

• Yashovarman built the Lakshmana temple and Dhanga built the Vishvanatha temple at Khajuraho, while Vidyadhara's Kandariya Mahadeva is the largest and most elaborate temple of the whole Khajuraho group.

 

NOTE

 

• Only 2 and 3 (Option 1): This combination keeps the false statement 3 and omits statement 1. The Chandelas ruled Bundelkhand, so statement 1 is true and must be included.

 

• Only 1 and 3 (Option 2): This combination includes statement 3 and omits statement 2. The Kandariya Mahadev temple was built by Vidyadhara, and statement 3 about the Dravida style is false.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): This combination claims all three are true, but the Khajuraho temples are Nagara in style, so statement 3 is false.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Sena dynasty:

1. Samant Sen was the founder of the dynasty.

2. The capital of the Senas was Kannauj.

3. The Senas ruled over Bengal after the Palas.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1 and 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statements 1 and 3 are accurate: Samant Sen founded the Sena dynasty, and the Senas ruled Bengal after the Palas; statement 2 is wrong because Kannauj was a Pratihara centre (सेन वंश — सामंत सेन, बंगाल)

 

• The Senas came to power as the Pala kingdom weakened in the eleventh and twelfth centuries.

 

• Their rule centred on the delta region of Bengal, with places such as Nadia and Vikrampur as centres.

 

• Kannauj was the capital of the Pratiharas under Mihir Bhoj and earlier of Harsha, so it cannot be a Sena capital.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vijayasena and Ballalasena were famous Sena kings.

 

• Lakshmanasena was the last important Sena ruler.

 

• The poet Jayadeva was at the court of Lakshmanasena.

 

• The Senas were displaced in Bengal by the Turkish invaders.

 

• Ballalasena wrote the Danasagara and Adbhutasagara and by tradition arranged the Kulin system among Bengal Brahmins and Kayasthas, while Vijayasena built up Sena power before him.

 

NOTE

 

• Only 1 and 2 (Option 2): This combination includes the false statement 2 and omits statement 3. Kannauj was not the Sena capital, and the Senas did rule Bengal after the Palas.

 

• Only 2 and 3 (Option 3): This combination keeps the false statement 2 and omits statement 1. Samant Sen did found the Sena dynasty, so statement 1 must be included.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): This combination says all three are correct, but statement 2 is false because Kannauj was never the Sena capital, and a choice accepting every statement must therefore be rejected.

question: Jayadeva, the author of the Gita Govinda, was a court poet of the Sena king:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lakshmanasena.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jayadeva, author of the Gita Govinda, adorned the court of the Sena king Lakshmanasena of Bengal (जयदेव — गीत गोविंद, लक्ष्मणसेन)

 

• The Gita Govinda is a lyrical Sanskrit poem on the love of Radha and Krishna and is a landmark of the Bhakti tradition in eastern India.

 

• Lakshmanasena was a late Sena king whose reign ended with the invasion of Bakhtiyar Khilji from the west in about 1204.

 

• The Senas followed the Palas as the main power in Bengal.

 

• Jayadeva's Gita Govinda has twelve cantos (sargas) and twenty-four songs (ashtapadis) and strongly influenced later Vaishnava devotion in Bengal and Odisha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Samant Sen is the founder of the dynasty.

 

• Vijayasena was a powerful ruler who expanded the kingdom.

 

• Ballalasena composed works like the Danasagara.

 

• Lakshmanasena's court also had poets such as Dhoyi and Halayudha.

 

• Lakshmanasena's capital Lakshmanavati (Lakhnauti) was in Gauda, and he is said to have left Nadia before Bakhtiyar Khilji and moved to eastern Bengal, where Sena rule lingered for a short while.

 

NOTE

 

• Samant Sen (Option 1): Samant Sen was the founder of the Sena line, living before the cultural flowering of the court of Lakshmanasena. He is not linked with Jayadeva.

 

• Vijayasena (Option 2): Vijayasena was the real builder of Sena power in Bengal but he preceded Lakshmanasena. Jayadeva belongs to the later court.

 

• Dharmapala (Option 3): Dharmapala was a Pala king and Pala rule had given way to the Senas by Jayadeva's time. He cannot be the patron of the poet.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Tomar dynasty of Delhi:

1. Aangpal (Anangapala) was its founder.

2. The Tomars were defeated by Prithviraj Chauhan.

3. The Tomars issued the famous Dehliwal coins in Delhi.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• All three statements are correct: Anangapala founded the Tomar line at Delhi, Prithviraj Chauhan later defeated the Tomars, and they issued the Dehliwal coins (तोमर वंश — अनंगपाल, दिल्लीवाल सिक्के)

 

• The Tomars are regarded as the early rulers of Delhi (Dhillika) before the Chauhans took it.

 

• The Dehliwal coins carried the name of the town and are a notable early medieval coinage of the region.

 

• After Prithviraj III lost the Second Battle of Tarain in 1192, Delhi passed to the Turks.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Anangapala is said to have laid out Lal Kot.

 

• Tomar rule in Delhi was succeeded by the Chauhans of Ajmer.

 

• Delhi became the Sultanate capital under Qutbuddin Aibak.

 

• Prithviraj Chauhan belonged to the Agnikula Chauhan clan.

 

• The iron pillar at Mehrauli is traditionally said to have been brought to Delhi by the Tomar king Anangapala, and Surajkund near Delhi is attributed to the Tomar ruler Surajpal.

 

NOTE

 

• Only 1 and 2 (Option 2): Statement 3 is true, so a choice that drops it is incomplete: the Tomars are indeed credited with issuing the Dehliwal coins in Delhi. It is therefore incomplete.

 

• Only 2 and 3 (Option 3): Dropping statement 1 fails because Aangpal is recorded in the notes as the founder of the Tomar dynasty. It is therefore incomplete.

 

• Only 1 and 3 (Option 4): A choice excluding statement 2 is also wrong, since the notes record that the Tomars were defeated by Prithviraj Chauhan. It is therefore incomplete.

question: The famous Sun Temple at Modhera in Gujarat was built by the Solanki ruler:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhimdev I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raja Bhimdev I of the Solanki dynasty built the Modhera Sun Temple in Gujarat (मोढेरा सूर्य मंदिर — भीमदेव प्रथम, सोलंकी)

 

• The Solankis are one of the four Agnikula clans and are linked with Gujarat in the notes.

 

• The temple is dedicated to Surya and is a fine example of the Nagara style of the early eleventh century.

 

• The Solanki capital was at Anhilwara (modern Patan).

 

• Modhera lies on the Pushpavati river in Mehsana district of Gujarat, and the temple has a sanctum, an assembly hall and a stepped tank in front, forming a complete Nagara plan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Konark Sun Temple in Odisha was built by the Eastern Ganga king Narasimhadeva I.

 

• The Martand Sun Temple in Kashmir was built by the Karkota king Lalitaditya.

 

• Mularaja is traditionally the founder of the Solanki dynasty.

 

• The Dilwara temples at Mount Abu were built in the Solanki period.

 

• The Modhera temple is built so that the first rays of the sun fall on the image of Surya at the equinoxes, and a stepped tank, Surya Kund, lies in front of the main shrine.

 

NOTE

 

• Mularaja (Option 1): Mularaja is traditionally regarded as the founder of the Solanki dynasty in Gujarat in the tenth century. The Modhera temple belongs to the later reign of Bhimdev I.

 

• Siddharaja Jayasimha (Option 2): Siddharaja Jayasimha was a famous Solanki ruler of the twelfth century, patron of Hemachandra, and builder of the Rudra Mahalaya. He is not the builder of the Modhera temple.

 

• Kumarapala (Option 3): Kumarapala was a Solanki king of the twelfth century who adopted Jainism under Hemachandra. The Sun Temple belongs to the earlier period of Bhimdev I.

question: Mahmud of Ghazni plundered the Somnath temple in 1025 AD during the reign of which Solanki king of Gujarat?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhima I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mahmud of Ghazni attacked Somnath in 1025 AD when the Solanki king Bhima I (Bhimdev I) ruled Gujarat; the same king is credited with the Modhera Sun Temple (सोमनाथ आक्रमण 1025 — भीम प्रथम)

 

• The Solankis were one of the Agnikula Rajput clans, associated with Gujarat.

 

• After Mahmud withdrew, Bhima I rebuilt the temple and recovered his kingdom, so Solanki power continued.

 

• Bhima I's reign also saw the building of the Dilwara temples at Mount Abu by his minister Vimala.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Somnath is on the coast of Saurashtra in Gujarat.

 

• Mahmud raided India seventeen times according to tradition.

 

• He also sacked Kannauj in 1018 AD in the time of the Pratihara ruler Rajyapala.

 

• Mahmud's court scholar Alberuni wrote Kitab-ul-Hind.

 

• Somnath on the Saurashtra coast is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Shiva, and Alberuni also refers to the temple in his Kitab-ul-Hind from the accounts that reached Ghazni.

 

NOTE

 

• Mularaja (Option 1): Mularaja founded the Solanki dynasty in the tenth century, almost eight decades before Mahmud's raid. He was not on the throne in 1025 AD.

 

• Kumarapala (Option 2): Kumarapala ruled in the twelfth century, over a hundred years after the Somnath raid. He is remembered for his Jain leanings.

 

• Siddharaja Jayasimha (Option 4): Siddharaja Jayasimha ruled in the late eleventh and early twelfth century, long after 1025 AD. He was not the king whose reign saw the attack.

question: Raja Bhoj, the famous ruler of the Parmar (Paramara) dynasty, who must not be confused with the Pratihara king Mihir Bhoj, ruled which region?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Malwa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raja Bhoj was the famous ruler of the Parmar (Paramara) dynasty of Malwa, with his capital at Dhar, and he is a different person from the Pratihara king Mihir Bhoj (राजा भोज — परमार वंश, मालवा)

 

• The Parmars are one of the four Agnikula clans and are associated with Malwa in the notes.

 

• Bhoj was celebrated as a patron of scholars and was himself a learned author.

 

• Mihir Bhoj ruled from Kannauj in the ninth century, while Raja Bhoj ruled in the eleventh century.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhoj is credited with works like the Samarangana Sutradhara.

 

• The Bhojshala at Dhar is linked with his name.

 

• Mihir Bhoj took the title Adivaraha.

 

• The Paramaras were rivals of the Chalukyas of Gujarat.

 

• Bhoj's uncle and predecessor Munja (Vakpati) was also a poet and patron of learning, and Bhoj's reign in the first half of the eleventh century is the high point of Paramara culture at Dhar.

 

NOTE

 

• Gujarat (Option 2): Gujarat was the land of the Solanki clan, whose capital was Anhilwara. Raja Bhoj of the Paramaras ruled in Malwa.

 

• Bengal (Option 3): Bengal was ruled by the Palas and Senas and was far from Dhar. It was not part of Bhoj's kingdom.

 

• Bundelkhand (Option 4): Bundelkhand was the Chandela territory, called Jejak Bhukti. It lay to the east of Malwa and was ruled by a different Rajput dynasty.

question: In the First Battle of Tarain (1191 AD), the Chauhan king Prithviraj III defeated:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muhammad Ghori.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the First Battle of Tarain (1191), Prithviraj III (Prithviraj Chauhan) defeated Muhammad Ghori, the ruler of Ghur; the Chauhans are the Agnikula clan linked with Ajmer (तराइन का प्रथम युद्ध 1191 — पृथ्वीराज चौहान की जीत)

 

• The victory was short-lived because Ghori returned in 1192 and won the Second Battle of Tarain, ending Prithviraj's reign.

 

• The defeat opened north India to Turkish rule, and Delhi soon became the seat of the Sultanate.

 

• Prithviraj also defeated the Tomars of Delhi, according to the notes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chandbardai's Prithviraj Raso narrates the exploits of Prithviraj.

 

• Ghori's general Qutbuddin Aibak later became the first Sultan of Delhi.

 

• Tarain is in present-day Haryana.

 

• Prithviraj Chauhan was also in conflict with the Chandelas.

 

• The First Battle of Tarain was fought near Karnal in present-day Haryana, and when Ghori returned in 1192 with a stronger cavalry and feigned retreat tactics he won the Second Battle of Tarain.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahmud of Ghazni (Option 1): Mahmud of Ghazni raided India about a century earlier, in the early eleventh century, and died in 1030. He was not Prithviraj's opponent at Tarain.

 

• Qutbuddin Aibak (Option 3): Qutbuddin Aibak was Ghori's slave and general who fought on his behalf, not the commander defeated at the First Battle of Tarain. He later became Sultan of Delhi.

 

• Jaichand (Option 4): Jaichand was the Gahadavala ruler of Kannauj, a rival of Prithviraj in Rajput politics. He was not the invader defeated at Tarain.

question: Mahipala I, the Pratihara king in whose reign Al-Masudi visited India, was the son of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahendrapala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mahipala I was the son of Mahendrapala and ruled the Pratihara kingdom in the early tenth century, when Al-Masudi visited India in 915 AD (महिपाल प्रथम — महेंद्रपाल का पुत्र)

 

• The line of descent runs Mihir Bhoj, Mahendrapala, Mahipala I, so Mahipala was the grandson of Mihir Bhoj.

 

• Mahendrapala I's reign is remembered for the court of the poet Rajashekhara at Kannauj.

 

• By Mahipala's time the empire began to weaken before Rashtrakuta raids on Kannauj.

 

• The Pratihara succession in this period ran from Mihir Bhoj to Mahendrapala I and then to Mahipala I, and knowing this order helps in questions on who was father or grandfather of whom.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mihir Bhoj ruled in the ninth century.

 

• Nagabhata II is known for capturing Kannauj.

 

• Vatsaraja was an eighth-century ruler defeated by Dhruva.

 

• Kannauj remained the Pratihara capital for a long time.

 

• In about 916 AD the Rashtrakuta king Indra III raided and plundered Kannauj in the time of Mahipala I, which weakened the Pratihara hold on the Gangetic plain.

 

NOTE

 

• Mihir Bhoj (Option 1): Mihir Bhoj was the grandfather of Mahipala I, not his father. Mahendrapala stood between them in the line, so Mahipala I was the grandson of Mihir Bhoj and not his son.

 

• Nagabhata II (Option 2): Nagabhata II belongs to the late eighth and early ninth century, before Mihir Bhoj. He was an earlier king and not Mahipala's father.

 

• Vatsaraja (Option 3): Vatsaraja ruled in the eighth century and was an ancestor of Mihir Bhoj. He was not the father of Mahipala I.

question:
Match the monuments or places with their dynasties:

(a) Khajuraho temples  (i) Solanki

(b) Modhera Sun Temple  (ii) Chandela

(c) Vikramashila University  (iii) Pala

(d) Kannauj under Mihir Bhoj  (iv) Gurjara-Pratihara
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct match is Khajuraho - Chandela, Modhera Sun Temple - Solanki, Vikramashila - Pala and Kannauj under Mihir Bhoj - Gurjara-Pratihara, i.e. a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv (स्मारक और राजवंश का मेल)

 

• The Chandelas ruled Jejak Bhukti (Bundelkhand) and the Solankis ruled Gujarat.

 

• The Palas of Bengal and Bihar patronised Vikramashila, founded by Dharmapala.

 

• The Pratiharas made Kannauj their capital under Mihir Bhoj, who defeated rivals in the tripartite struggle.

 

• The match covers four regions: Bundelkhand for the Chandelas, Gujarat for the Solankis, Bihar for the Palas and Kannauj in Uttar Pradesh for the Pratiharas, each with its own monument or centre.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Khajuraho is in Madhya Pradesh.

 

• Modhera is in Gujarat.

 

• Vikramashila was located in Bihar.

 

• Kannauj is in Uttar Pradesh.

 

• Khajuraho was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986, and the ruins of the Nalanda Mahavihara were inscribed in 2016, which shows the lasting importance of these early medieval monuments for culture and tourism.

 

NOTE

 

• a-i, b-ii, c-iv, d-iii (Option 2): This combination gives Khajuraho to the Solankis and Modhera to the Chandelas, a reversal, and also swaps Vikramashila with Kannauj. Khajuraho is Chandela and Modhera is Solanki.

 

• a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i (Option 3): This combination gives Khajuraho to the Palas and Vikramashila to the Chandelas, which is wrong. Vikramashila belongs to the Palas and Khajuraho to the Chandelas.

 

• a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv (Option 4): This combination keeps Khajuraho with the Chandelas but gives Modhera to the Palas and Vikramashila to the Solankis. Modhera is Solanki and Vikramashila is Pala.
